plan.planning_summary: This is a dichroic filter design problem: high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm (quantum signal) with high reflectance at 400-700 nm (solar background rejection). The literature provides strong support for HfO2/SiO2 as a material pair (L04, L07, L16, L25, L28, L34, L40) and the cold mirror concept (L33) directly matches this spectral requirement. Four genuinely distinct strategy axes are proposed: (1) periodic Bragg stack testing classic cold mirror design, (2) aperiodic thickness-optimized stack testing whether breaking periodicity improves band-edge sharpness, (3) AR-matched Bragg stack testing whether impedance matching reduces passband ripple, and (4) chirped Bragg stack testing whether thickness grading broadens the reflection band. Each route has one fixed topology and one distinct design variable, ensuring comparable iteration results.

routes.title: Periodic Quarter-Wave Bragg Cold Mirror
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave Bragg stack with center wavelength tuned to the visible band will achieve high reflectance at 400-700 nm while maintaining high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm.
routes.design_principle: Bragg interference from periodic high-low index pairs creates a photonic bandgap centered at the quarter-wave wavelength. L33 demonstrates this cold mirror concept with TiO2/SiO2; HfO2/SiO2 (L04, L07, L34) provides similar index contrast with better space qualification.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (10 pairs, 20 layers total)
design_variables: quarter-wave reference wavelength (tunes all layer thicknesses proportionally)
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are space-qualified materials (L07, L25, L28)
Quarter-wave thicknesses are manufacturable with standard deposition
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Bragg condition: optical thickness = λ/4 at center wavelength
Index contrast determines bandgap width and reflectance magnitude
expected_advantages: Predictable spectral position from quarter-wave wavelength
L33 validates cold mirror concept for visible-reflect/IR-transmit
known_risks: Periodic structure may have limited band-edge sharpness
Passband ripple from impedance mismatch at air interface
May not achieve both bands simultaneously with fixed pair count

routes.design_principle: Needle optimization and aperiodic designs (L34 mentions needle optimization for HfO2/SiO2) can achieve spectral shapes unattainable with fixed periodicity. L09 demonstrates RL-driven multi-objective optimization for composite thin films.

routes.title: AR-Matched Bragg Stack with Impedance Grading
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Adding anti-reflection matching layers at the air interface will reduce passband ripple in the 1530-1565 nm transmission band while maintaining visible band reflectance.
routes.design_principle: Impedance mismatch at air-dielectric interface causes passband ripple. L13 demonstrates Al2O3/SiO2 AR coatings; L22 shows quarter-wave AR layers improve transmission bandwidth. SiO2 AR layers can grade the index transition.

Layer count fixed at 20. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand).

routes.title: Chirped Bragg Stack for Broadened Reflection Band
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A chirped Bragg stack with gradually increasing layer thicknesses will broaden the 400-700 nm reflection band compared to uniform quarter-wave design, improving solar background rejection across the full visible spectrum.
routes.design_principle: Chirped structures (varying period through the stack) create multiple overlapping bandgaps, broadening the reflection band. L06 mentions thickness-modulated multilayer filters for spectral shaping. This addresses the challenge of covering 400-700 nm (300 nm bandwidth) with a single periodic design.
